_readme: Every screenshot in docs/tutorials/*.md is declared here and captured from the live product by scripts/capture-guide-shots.mjs. Add a shot, run the capture, run sync:guide-media. Never hand-place an image in a tutorial: check:guide-media fails on anything this file does not describe. See docs/guide-media.md.

callouts.note: **Describe it** is the text-to-3D tab, and the one the Forge opens on.
The prompt box. One object, one material, no scenery.
**Surprise me** fills the box with a known-good prompt; **Enhance** rewrites yours into a richer one.
Quality tier. Draft and Standard are free for everyone.
Generate. Results stream into the stage on the right.

shots.alt: The three.ws Forge compose panel, with the Describe it tab, prompt box, Surprise me and Enhance buttons, the quality tier row, and the Generate button each marked with a numbered callout.
shots.caption: The Forge compose panel. Everything you need for a text-to-3D run is in this one column.

callouts.note: Draft, Standard and High. Start on Draft or Standard, then re-run the winning prompt on High.
The engine row. Lanes marked FREE need no key and no account.

shots.alt: The Forge quality panel showing the Draft, Standard and High tier buttons above a row of generation engines, several labelled FREE, with numbered callouts on the tier row and the engine row.
shots.caption: Tier and engine sit together: tier decides how much detail you get, engine decides who renders it.

placements.anchor: Step 3 — Pick a tier (both free lanes)

shots.alt: The Forge stage panel, the large viewport where a finished 3D model is displayed and can be orbited.
shots.caption: The stage. Finished models land here and can be orbited, zoomed and downloaded without leaving the page.

callouts.note: **From photos** switches the Forge into photo-to-3D mode.
Drop up to six photos of the same object here, taken from different angles.
The view counter. More angles means a more complete reconstruction.

shots.alt: The Forge in photo mode, showing the From photos tab selected, an empty grid of reference view slots, and a view counter, each marked with a numbered callout.
shots.caption: Photo mode. The same panel, swapped from a prompt box to a reference-photo grid.

placements.anchor: Step 2 — Open the Forge in photo mode

callouts.note: Expands the list to the full set of worked example prompts.

shots.alt: A row of example prompt chips beneath the Forge prompt box, each one a complete ready-to-run prompt, with a callout on the button that reveals more.
shots.caption: Example chips are complete prompts, not keywords. Tap one to load it, then edit a word or two.

callouts.note: Start from a ready-made avatar. Fastest route to something on screen.
Describe the character you want and have it generated.
Turn a selfie into an avatar.
Bring a GLB you already have.

shots.alt: The three.ws create page showing the avatar option cards: start from a default avatar, describe one, use a selfie, or upload a GLB, each marked with a numbered callout.
shots.caption: Every route to an avatar starts here. They all end in the same editor, so the choice is reversible.

callouts.note: The avatar gallery. Pick a body without leaving the page.
Live preview. It renders the real widget, not a picture of one.
Widget settings. Every change re-renders the preview immediately.
Produces the embed snippet to paste into your site.

shots.alt: The three.ws Widget Studio, a three-column workbench with an avatar gallery on the left, a live widget preview in the middle, and a configuration form on the right, with numbered callouts on each.
shots.caption: Widget Studio: pick on the left, watch in the middle, configure on the right, and leave with an embed snippet.

callouts.note: Talk to the agent in plain language. It answers in character and moves while it does.
Suggested openers, so an empty input is never a dead end.

shots.alt: The chat dock in the three.ws viewer, with a message input and a row of suggested opening prompts, each marked with a numbered callout.
shots.caption: The chat dock. Suggested prompts mean a first-time visitor never has to guess what to type.

callouts.note: Browse the animation library and play any clip on the current avatar. Keyboard: `A`.
Swap the avatar. The scene keeps its camera and backdrop.
Change the backdrop behind the agent.

shots.alt: The secondary action bar in the three.ws viewer with Animations, Avatar and Backdrop buttons, each marked with a numbered callout.
shots.caption: The action bar. Animations, avatar and backdrop are the three things worth changing first.

callouts.note: Search filters the whole documentation tree as you type.

shots.alt: The three.ws documentation sidebar, with a search box above a long navigation tree of sections, and a callout on the search box.
shots.caption: The docs sidebar. Searching filters the tree in place rather than sending you to a results page.

placements.anchor: Use the index instead of walking

callouts.note: Search across every published agent.
Reorder the index. Useful for finding recently published agents.

shots.alt: The header of the three.ws agents index, with a wide search field and a sort selector, each marked with a numbered callout.
shots.caption: The public agents index. Your agent appears here once it is published, and this is the page visitors search.

placements.anchor: Step 1 — Find your agent's public URL
